statements.label: thm:r74-low-contrast
statements.title: Attainment of the module bound at small contrast
hypotheses: Nonconstant compactly reversible finite-dimensional probability response with finite minimal observable group G
Arbitrary finite terminal outcome set
pi is the group average and b_t=pi+t(b-pi), 0<=t<=1; outputs with pi_c=0 are identically zero and may be restored as zero decoder columns
statements.conclusion: For an explicit t0>0, kappa_G(b_t)=nu_G(V_b) and m(b_t)=min{N,1+nu_G(V_b)} for every 0<t<=t0. The observable group, module and residual count are unchanged for all t>0. At t=0 memory is one.
statements.proof: Separate the invariant constant response from its zero-average module W. Embed W equivariantly into a minimum permutation module, project back using its invariant inner product, perturb a uniform preparation, and scale the decoder. epsilon=1/(2k||a||infty), B=max|T_xc|/pi_c and t0=min{1,epsilon/B} ensure positivity. An invertible equivariant residual map proves the unchanged invariants and matching lower.
classical_ingredients: Averaging and invariant inner products for finite group representations
statements.claim_class: Exact permutation-module saturation with one common command action and the inherited pure-start charge; not the invention of equivariance or mixing-based positivity.
statements.limits: Terminal readout contrast is not channel damping; t=0 is a separate degenerate observable quotient. No A1/A2 or general Theta completion follows.

statements.label: thm:r74-contrast-thresholds
statements.title: Attained exact contrast thresholds
hypotheses: The finite-G contrast family and minimal observable group of thm:r74-low-contrast
Integer budget k>=1
Algebraic or rational data only for the respective effective arithmetic assertions
statements.conclusion: The feasible contrasts for kappa<=k are exactly [0,tau_k], with attained endpoints, monotone budget thresholds, tau_N=1, tau_k=0 below nu and tau_nu>0. Only finitely many positive-contrast memory transitions occur. Algebraic data give computable algebraic endpoints; Dedekind groups give finitely many LPs and rational endpoints/controllers for rational data.
statements.proof: For each of finitely many actions of size at most k, probability parameters form a compact set with closed polynomial response constraints. Decoder mixing fills the initial interval and compactness retains its endpoint. The remaining arithmetic assertion is classical real QE, or the exact normal-subgroup LP reduction.
statements.claim_class: Structure of the exact resource thresholds for this group-response invariant.
statements.limits: No efficient general algorithm or executed general QE solve is asserted. Rationality of endpoints is not claimed for arbitrary nonabelian groups.

statements.label: prop:r74-s3-contrast
statements.title: An exact qubit readout threshold
hypotheses: The retained prepared-qubit S3 response with u=(1,-1,0)
beta_t(g)=1/2+(t/4)uP_gu^T and binary bounded decoder
0<t<=1; prescribed pure start for m
statements.conclusion: d=3 and N=6 throughout positive contrast. Core size is 3 up to and including t=2/3 and 6 above it; exact pure-start size is respectively 4 and 6. At zero contrast memory is one.
statements.proof: Every faithful S3-set of size<=5 has one natural orbit and only trivial/sign extras. Remove those coefficient components; four displayed matrices span End(R^2), forcing preparation and decoder contrasts parallel to u. Probability bounds imply t<=2/3. Explicit three-point decoder and the six-residual machine match both intervals.
classical_ingredients: Elementary S3 representation and orbit structure
statements.claim_class: New exact contrast law for the retained model, not a new claim for its already established full-contrast obstruction.
statements.limits: Special qubit/S3 family, not a universal nonabelian closed formula.

statements.label: lem:r74-normal-orbits
statements.title: Absorption of within-orbit preparation
hypotheses: Finite G-set probability factorization b(g)=lambda P_gD
Every orbit stabilizer in this factorization is normal
statements.conclusion: Without increasing size, preparation is supported at the identity coset of each quotient and there is at most one orbit of each subgroup type. Only a mixture across different quotient orbits remains.
statements.proof: Normality makes the local mixed-orbit response H-invariant, hence itself a legal quotient decoder. Merge repeated quotient types using their orbit masses and delete zero-mass orbits.
statements.claim_class: Size-preserving elimination of the within-orbit bilinearity in this resource problem.
statements.limits: The lemma is not asserted for nonnormal stabilizers. A finite S3 negative control explicitly demonstrates the failed invariance in that case.

statements.label: thm:r74-quotient-lp
statements.title: Exact quotient linear programs
hypotheses: Finite minimal observable Dedekind group G: every subgroup is normal
Arbitrary response probability table on G and finite output set
Coefficient field assumptions only for rational/algebraic realization claims
statements.conclusion: kappa is the minimum sum of subgroup indices over distinct nonempty subgroup families satisfying the displayed nonnegative quotient-table linear equations. N=|G|, and m=min{|G|,1+kappa}. Rational tables have rational optimal controllers; data in a real algebraic number field admit optimal controllers in the same field.
statements.proof: Absorption proves necessity; quotient-point preparations and f_H/p_H decoders prove sufficiency. A normal initial-residual stabilizer fixes the whole observable span and is trivial. Every feasible bounded polyhedron has a vertex over its coefficient field.
statements.claim_class: Exact linear reduction for normal quotient orbits with unchanged label resource.
statements.limits: Subgroup-family selection is finite but not claimed polynomial; arbitrary nonnormal G actions remain bilinear.

statements.label: thm:r74-quotient-dual
statements.title: Payoff certificates and exact contrast endpoints
hypotheses: A nonempty distinct subgroup family in the finite Dedekind setting
Payoff pairing is the unnormalized sum over G times the finite output set
The endpoint formula uses nonconstant v=b-pi and pi equal to the group average
statements.conclusion: Feasibility is equivalent to all displayed payoff support inequalities. Infeasibility has a strict rational witness and a norm-controlled perturbation margin. The exact contrast endpoint equals the attained primal LP and the displayed normalized support-function dual; rational input gives rational endpoints and controllers.
statements.proof: The feasible set is the convex hull of quotient probability polytopes. Compute its support function cosetwise. Closest-point separation supplies a strict witness, rational approximation preserves the gap, and the l1 bound controls perturbations. Affine-hull equations or a reached facet prove dual attainment even without strict feasibility.
statements.claim_class: An explicit exact dual for the quotient memory optimization and its resource thresholds.
statements.limits: This is not a general black-box Farkas proof for arbitrary nonabelian factorizations; no general solver run is claimed.

statements.label: cor:r74-abelian-cover
statements.title: The abelian module cover
hypotheses: Finite abelian observable G
Active complex character set consists of the nonzero vector Fourier coefficients of b, including the trivial mode and closed under conjugation
statements.conclusion: nu is the least sum of subgroup indices whose annihilators cover all active characters. This equals kappa at every sufficiently small positive contrast, but can fail at full contrast.
statements.proof: The cyclic abelian module has each active complex character once; quotient permutation modules have precisely the characters trivial on their stabilizer. Real conjugate pairs are counted as their two-dimensional real summands.
statements.claim_class: Classical representation cover identified with the exact low-contrast stochastic resource.
statements.limits: No claim that the character-cover computation or abelian representation decomposition itself is new.

statements.label: prop:r74-circuit-transition
statements.title: A sharp transition invisible to the observable module
hypotheses: G=(F2)^4 with coordinate generator commands
chi_5=chi_1 chi_2 chi_3 chi_4 and beta_t=3/8+(t/8)sum_{i=1}^5 chi_i
Binary response, 0<t<=1, bounded probability decoder
statements.conclusion: The fixed invariants are d=6, N=16, nu=10. kappa is 10 for 0<t<=3/5 and 12 for 3/5<t<=1; pure-start memory is respectively 11 and 13. At zero contrast it is one.
statements.proof: Any four of the five characters are independent. All actions of budget<=11 must partition the active modes into singleton/pair quotient blocks. The explicit witness z=1-sum chi_i+sum_pair chi_i chi_j has nonnegative quotient averages but target pairing (3-5t)/8. Five binary quotient decoders and a four-plus-eight point indicator/majority construction match both regions.
statements.claim_class: New sharp positivity threshold with matching construction and unchanged observable invariants.
statements.limits: Special sixteen-point group family; its physical realization is already classical, so no quantum advantage is claimed.

statements.label: cor:r74-circuit-robust
statements.title: A robust finite-table obstruction
hypotheses: A binary probability table on the same G=(F2)^4 and the same command quotient
Sup norm distance from beta_t is strictly less than (5t-3)/18
statements.conclusion: The perturbed table still requires kappa>=12 and prescribed-start memory>=13.
statements.proof: The perturbation is smaller than t/8, retaining all five active modes, faithfulness and N=16. All small actions have the same partition type. Their witnesses have normalized l1 norm at most 9/4, so the exact negative margin survives.
statements.claim_class: Quantified lower certificate from the exact circuit dual witnesses.
statements.limits: Sufficient radius only; not a sharp neighbourhood or a matching upper for arbitrary perturbed tables. No statement about perturbing the command dynamics outside this fixed quotient.

statements.label: thm:r74-contraction
statements.title: A common contracting realization
hypotheses: Finite nonempty command and output sets; linear response b(w,c)=p_c+ell_c(x_w), x_{wa}=F_a x_w
All actual word responses are probabilities; p is a probability row and sum_c ell_c=0
A supplied common norm, 0<rho<1 and r>0 obey ||F_a x||<=rho||x|| and r||ell_c||_*<=p_c
Choose T>=1 with rho^(T-1)||x0||<=r
statements.conclusion: One bounded-decoder stochastic machine from a prescribed pure start realizes every mixed command word on at most sum_{j=0}^{T-1}|A|^j+ceil((1+2/(1-rho))^n) labels. A supplied uniform exponentially decaying product bound implies such a common norm. A constant response needs one label.
statements.proof: A maximal norm-net produces rho B subset conv(V) subset B, making r conv(V) invariant for every command. Prefix-tree transient labels enter this common polytope at depth T. Barycentric transition rows preserve represented vectors and all legal decoder rows. The product-bound norm is an explicitly bounded supremum over words.
statements.claim_class: A quantified constructive consequence of the classical invariant-polytope mechanism: arbitrary finite mixed-command linear responses, a supplied norm and explicit transient/core counts. It is not a new positive-realization principle.
statements.limits: Sufficient certificate and explicit upper only; no minimum, efficient net synthesis, joint spectral-radius decision procedure, or finite exact-sampling complexity assertion. The proof is a quantified corollary of the established invariant-polytope framework; no broad novelty claim is attached to existence alone.

statements.label: thm:r74-depolarizing-obstruction
statements.title: Exact memory in a uniformly positive one-dependent family
hypotheses: The three displayed qubit branches Psi0=Ad(Utheta)/8, Psi1=tr(EX)tau/4 and Psi2=D-Psi0-Psi1
sin(theta)!=0 and known initial state I/2
All classical candidate models use arbitrary nonnegative outcome matrices whose sum is row-stochastic
statements.conclusion: The instrument is CP with uniformly positive outcome probabilities and exactly depolarizing average channel. Its stationary output is one-dependent and has Hankel rank three. For phase order q>=3 the exact free-mixed-start count is q and exact prescribed-pure-start count q+1; for non-root phase no finite model exists. Algebraic sin/cos give algebraic superoperators, including a rational-superoperator infinite example.
statements.proof: A uniform Choi lower bound proves CP. The averaged reset proves one-dependence. The cylinders 1 0^n 1 have three nonzero exponential modes. Active-path inequalities bound the relevant nonnegative matrix radius; Perron normalization and the peripheral eigenvector equality force cycles divisible by q. Regular physical q-gons give the matching upper. At equality q, pure initialization forces a constant-weight q-cycle and constant outcome-one column, contradicting the oscillatory cylinder.
statements.claim_class: The simultaneous fixed-qubit, rank-three, three uniformly positive outcome, exactly depolarizing average and one-dependent properties, together with the sharp prescribed-pure-start increment q to q+1. Phase-order/infinite-memory phenomena and the peripheral-spectrum mechanism have the FRDN antecedents explicitly discussed in Fanizza24 Section 2.3.
statements.limits: No first-existence claim for one-dependent non-HMM processes or phase-order/infinite-memory dichotomies. The counterexample distinguishes average mixing from posterior mixing and does not weaken the inherited thm:r68-instrument.

statements.label: cor:r74-period-four-closed
statements.title: Inherited complete four-period count
hypotheses: b_alpha(n)=(1+alpha^n cos(pi n/2))/2 for n>=0 and 0<=alpha<=1
Prescribed pure initial label and bounded randomized decoder
statements.conclusion: Exact memory is 2 at alpha=0, 3 for 0<alpha<=1/sqrt(3), and 4 for 1/sqrt(3)<alpha<=1.
statements.proof: Apply the inherited first-sector theorem with M=3 and theta=pi/2, use the three-mode rank lower, and retain the damped four-cycle upper. At alpha=0 the initial probability differs from the constant tail, requiring two labels.
classical_ingredients: Inherited spectral threshold and explicit cycle realization
statements.claim_class: Inherited logical closure, explicitly not counted as a new independent spectral theorem.
statements.limits: Corrects the status of this family's first transition; other damping transitions and the finite-probe certificate remain different questions.
